subs.en: One GPU. 24 GB. Your model needs 22. The last 2 sit empty.
Slicing can't help: slices come in fixed sizes, and none leaves a 2 GB corner.
So the small model gets a GPU of its own.
It keeps a memory ledger and packs each GPU by size.
Generative, predictive, embeddings: different engines, different sizes, same GPU.
One proxy routes every request to the right model.
More models than memory? The idle ones sleep in host RAM.
A request for a sleeping model is parked while the least recently used one is swapped out.
The client just sees a slow first token.
